title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: these are notes for a 1976 IHÉS talk on the divided-power (PD) de Rham complex. The neighbouring 'pages' are typescript pages 188–189 of SGA 7 Exposé IX (biextensions, rigid-analytic uniformisation). They are evidently the scrap paper this was written on and are unrelated to the content.

Setup. Take a ring S with a PD-ideal (S^{[1]}, γ) and an element t, implicitly in the PD-ideal. For each n, let Â_n^0 be the completed PD-polynomial algebra S{{X_0,…,X_n}} modulo the closed PD-ideal generated by ΣX_i − t. Geometrically this is the ring of PD-functions on the 'algebraic n-simplex of size t', {ΣX_i = t}. Set Â_n^* = Â_n^0 ⊗_S Λ^*[dX_0,…,dX_n]/(ΣdX_i), its PD de Rham complex. Eliminating one variable gives Â_n^* ≅ S{{Y_1,…,Y_n}}[dY_1,…,dY_n]. As n varies, with face maps restricting to faces (X_j ↦ 0) and degeneracies X_j ↦ X_j + X_{j+1}, this is a simplicial commutative DG-algebra. It is the PD/integral analogue of Sullivan's simplicial algebra of polynomial forms ∇(•,*), with an extra parameter t.

Step 1 (reduction to degree 0). Write Y_*^S for the simplicial S-module of linear forms (dX_i modulo ΣdX_i). Then Â^i_* ≅ Â^0_* ⊗_S Λ^i(Y_*^S). The normalisation of Y^S is S in degree 1, so Y^S ≃ K(S,1). By décalage, LΛ^i(M[1]) ≃ LΓ^i(M)[i], hence Λ^i(Y^S) ≃ K(Γ^i S, i) = K(S,i). Künneth then gives π_ℓ(Â^i_*) ≅ π_{ℓ−i}(Â^0_*). So everything reduces to computing π_*(Â^0_*).

Step 2 (filtration). Put on Â^0_n the decreasing filtration by closed PD-ideals generated by giving the X_i and t filtration ≥ 1:
- Fil^p = {Σ a_I X^{[I]} : a_I ∈ S^{[p−|I|]}}.
- Â^0_n is separated and complete for this filtration.

Step 3 (graded pieces). Put k = S/S^{[1]}, and assume the map from the PD-polynomial algebra k⟨T⟩ (t ↦ T) to Gr^*(S) is an isomorphism. Then Gr^p(Â^0_*) ≅ Γ^p_k(Φ^k_*), where Φ_n = k^{n+1} spanned by X_0,…,X_n (T = ΣX_i). Equivalently, Gr is the same construction over (Gr S, γ̃, T̃).
- Check: the normalised complex of Φ is kX_1 → kX_0, an isomorphism, so Φ is contractible.
- By Dold–Puppe, Γ^p_k of a contractible simplicial module is contractible for p ≥ 1.
- Hence π_i Gr^p = 0 for p ≠ 0, and π_0 Gr^0 = k. This is exactly the page's claim.

Conclusion (left unfinished on the page). By completeness, Â^0_* ≃ k (constant) and π_ℓ(Â^i_*) = k for ℓ = i, 0 otherwise. Consistently, in π_0 one has t ~ 0: the element X_0 ∈ Â_1 has faces t and 0. So the t-simplices, with t in the PD-ideal, contract S onto S/S^{[1]}. This is a crystalline-flavoured 'PD Poincaré lemma on simplices', valid in all characteristics. It is presumably meant as the key acyclicity input for an integral/PD de Rham theorem (simplicial PD forms computing cohomology of simplicial sets), parallel to Cartan's 1976 divided-power 'théories cohomologiques'.
errors: Step 1 silently uses flatness/Künneth and the décalage Λ^i(K(S,1)) ≃ K(S,i). These are correct, but not justified on the page.
The final deduction from the graded pieces to the completed filtered object (a lim/lim^1 argument) is not written; the concluding line is struck out and left unfinished.

The page states π_0(Gr^0) = k but does not draw the consequence that π_0(Â^0_*) is k = S/S^{[1]}, not S. The constants t^{[p]} die in homotopy because t is simplicially homotopic to 0. This is worth stating explicitly.
The hypothesis Gr^*(S) ≅ k⟨T⟩ is quite restrictive and is only marked by an arrow ('si … est un iso'). Its role (needed to identify Gr^p as Γ^p(Φ)) is not discussed.

ideas.what: Simplicial DG-algebra of completed PD-polynomial differential forms on algebraic simplices {ΣX_i = t}
ideas.modern_name: Divided-power analogue of Sullivan's simplicial polynomial de Rham algebra; integral/PD forms on simplices
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan (1977) for the rational version; H. Cartan, 'Théories cohomologiques' (1976) for divided-power forms; Cenkl–Porter (c. 1980) for integral de Rham theorems

ideas.what: Reduction π_ℓ(Â^i) ≅ π_{ℓ−i}(Â^0) via Λ^i(K(S,1)) ≃ K(S,i)
PD-adic filtration with Gr^p ≅ Γ^p_k(Φ), Φ contractible, giving acyclicity
ideas.modern_name: Filtration argument / Dold–Puppe non-additive functors applied to a contractible simplicial module

ideas.what: Simplices of 'size t' with t in a PD-ideal, contracting S to S/S^{[1]} homotopically
ideas.modern_name: Simplicial model of PD-thickening / crystalline-type Poincaré lemma

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a t-parametrised PD de Rham algebra on simplices over a PD-ring and computes its homotopy via the PD filtration. The conclusion, that Â^0_* ≃ S/S^{[1]} and Â^i_* ≃ K(k,i), is left unwritten. This is part of an unpublished 1976 programme for an integral/PD de Rham theory of simplicial objects, contemporaneous with Cartan's divided-power forms.
missed.quote: On considère sur Â_*^0 la filtration décroissante par idéaux fermés stables par p.d. … Gr^p(Â_*^0) ≃ Γ^p_k(Φ_*^k)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral models of homotopy types are an active topic (schematisation revisited by Toën; Horel; Yuan; Mandell). So does PD/derived de Rham à la Bhatt. A deformation parameter t in a PD-ideal, making simplices 'infinitesimally small', is a slightly unusual feature that links simplicial de Rham models to crystalline thickenings.

missed.claim: The construction implicitly links Sullivan/Cartan simplicial forms with crystalline PD-envelopes: the size-t simplex over a PD-base computes the reduction mod the PD-ideal.
missed.quote: posant k = S/S^{[1]} … si l'op. k[T]→Gr^*(S) est un iso
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is suggestive of a crystalline/derived-de-Rham approach to integral homotopy theory. As far as I know it is not attributed to Grothendieck, but similar computations exist in the integral de Rham literature, so novelty is modest.

deep.surprise_reason: The page documents an unpublished Grothendieck computation in 1976: PD de Rham forms on simplices, with a PD-parameter t. This is historically notable as evidence of his early interest in integral de Rham models of homotopy types. The mathematics itself is a fairly routine filtration/décalage computation, and close analogues exist in Cartan (1976) and later integral de Rham work.
transcription_corrections: Top line: the object reads Â_*^*(S, γ^*, t)^∧ (parameters S, PD-structure γ, element t); the reading '(S,γ*,1)' in the image hand is ambiguous, and t is the later-used parameter.
'Λ Y_*^S' is Λ^*(Y_*^S), and in the next line Λ^i(Y_*^S).
'si l'op. k[T]→Gr^*(S)' is likely 'si l'app.' (application) and k[T] probably denotes the PD-polynomial algebra k⟨T⟩.
The marginal annotation reads roughly '≃ Â_*^{p,0}(Gr^*(S), γ̃^*, t̃)', with a gloss 'composante graduée p-ième, gr. module de k⟨T⟩'.
The verso material (pp. 188–189, numbered 506–507) is typescript of SGA 7 Exposé IX, unrelated to this page's content.
